definitions.explanation: Describes information or news that is pleasant, useful, or beneficial to the listener. Literally suggests something that 'comes to the ear' — news that you'd want to hear.

examples.japanese: {耳寄|みみよ}りな{情報|じょうほう}がある。
examples.english: I have some interesting news for you.

examples.japanese: {旅行者|りょこうしゃ}には{耳寄|みみよ}りな{話|はなし}だ。
examples.english: This is welcome news for travelers.

examples.japanese: {節約|せつやく}したい{人|ひと}に{耳寄|みみよ}りなキャンペーンが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: A campaign with great news for people who want to save money has started.

notes:
Literally "ear-approaching" — information that naturally draws your attention because it is beneficial or interesting. Almost always used to modify {話|はなし} (story/news) or {情報|じょうほう} (information).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {耳寄|みみよ}りな{話|はなし}: interesting/welcome news
- {耳寄|みみよ}りな{情報|じょうほう}: useful information
- {耳寄|みみよ}りなニュース: welcome news
- {耳寄|みみよ}りなお{知|し}らせ: a welcome announcement

USAGE:
Frequently used in advertising, news headlines, and promotional materials to attract attention. The nuance is that the information will benefit the listener — a deal, a tip, or good news.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{得|とく}な: bargain, good deal — focuses on financial benefit
- {朗報|ろうほう}: good news — more formal, used in news reporting
- {有益|ゆうえき}な: beneficial, useful — more formal and objective
